title: Sanctions Compliance
summary: An eight-module practitioner programme on designing and running effective sanctions compliance, from ownership and screening to evasion typologies, licensing and breach reporting.
intro: This training programme equips compliance, MLRO, operations and front-office staff to design and run an effective sanctions compliance framework: understanding the regimes, screening and investigating effectively, detecting evasion and evidencing sound controls to supervisors.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To equip practitioners with a working understanding of how financial sanctions and related trade controls operate, and the practical controls needed to comply with them across clients, payments and transactions. Participants leave able to apply ownership and control tests, manage screening and alerts, recognise evasion, handle licences and frozen assets, and evidence a sound framework to supervisors.
sections.What It Covers: How sanctions regimes work, ownership and control, name, payment and vessel screening, evasion typologies including trade-based and crypto-asset evasion, export controls and dual-use goods, correspondent banking and payments, licensing and frozen assets, investigations and breach reporting, and governance, assurance and testing.
Intended Audience: Compliance officers, MLROs, sanctions specialists and financial crime analysts
Payments, operations, trade finance and client onboarding staff who handle screening alerts or transactions
Front-office, relationship and product staff in firms with cross-border clients, payments or trade exposure
Learning Objectives: Explain how UN, regional and national sanctions regimes are made, applied and enforced
Apply ownership and control tests and identify indirect exposure to designated persons
Design and calibrate screening of clients, payments, vessels and counterparties
Recognise evasion typologies, including trade-based, maritime and crypto-asset evasion
Manage licences, frozen assets, investigations and the reporting of breaches
Evaluate the firm's sanctions governance, testing and assurance, and agree improvements
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a three- to four-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a short briefing with case studies, typologies and practical screening exercises, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's business and exposure.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial crime compliance, payments or client onboarding is helpful. No prior specialist sanctions knowledge is required.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)
FSB, Enhancing Cross-border Payments: Stage 3 Roadmap (2020)
Basel Committee, Compliance and the Compliance Function in Banks (2005)

modules.title: How Sanctions Regimes Work
modules.summary: The architecture of financial sanctions: who imposes them, the main types of measure, how lists are maintained and updated, and why sanctions obligations differ from anti-money laundering obligations.
objectives: Explain the roles of UN, regional and national sanctions authorities
Distinguish asset freezes, financial, sectoral and trade restrictions
Identify the regimes that apply to the firm through nationality, currency and location
syllabus: Purpose and policy objectives of sanctions, and how designations are made
Types of measure: asset freezes, sectoral, investment, services and trade restrictions
Jurisdictional reach: nationality, territory, currency and extraterritorial effect
Strict liability, criminal and civil enforcement, and reputational consequences

modules.title: Ownership, Control and Indirect Exposure
modules.summary: How sanctions extend beyond listed names to entities owned or controlled by designated persons, and how firms identify and evidence indirect exposure through complex structures.
objectives: Apply aggregate ownership and control tests to corporate structures
Identify control through nominees, trusts, family members and contractual rights
Document ownership and control decisions defensibly
syllabus: Ownership thresholds, aggregation and the meaning of control
Making funds available indirectly: the prohibition and its practical scope
Opaque structures, nominees, divestments and restructurings designed to evade
Exercise: mapping a complex ownership chain

modules.title: Screening Clients, Payments and Vessels
modules.summary: Designing, calibrating and operating screening across clients, counterparties, payments, securities and vessels, and managing alerts consistently and at scale.
objectives: Design a screening framework proportionate to the firm's exposure
Calibrate fuzzy matching, list coverage and thresholds, and justify the settings
Disposition alerts consistently with a clear audit trail
syllabus: Customer, counterparty, payment and securities screening: what, when and against which lists
Fuzzy matching, transliteration, thresholds and false-positive management
Vessel, port and trade document screening
Exercise: dispositioning a set of screening alerts

modules.title: Evasion Typologies: Trade, Maritime and Crypto-Assets
modules.summary: How designated persons and states evade sanctions through front companies, trade, shipping and crypto-assets, and the red flags that should prompt investigation.
objectives: Recognise common evasion techniques and the red flags they leave
Identify trade-based and maritime evasion, including transhipment and vessel deception
Assess crypto-asset evasion risk and the blockchain analytics used to detect it
syllabus: Front companies, intermediaries, third-country transhipment and wire stripping
Maritime deception: flag hopping, transponder manipulation and ship-to-ship transfers
Crypto-asset evasion: mixers, exchanges in high-risk jurisdictions and wallet screening
Case studies of evasion schemes and the controls that missed them

modules.title: Export Controls, Dual-Use Goods and Trade Finance
modules.summary: Where trade and export controls overlap with financial sanctions, the role of the financial sector in preventing proliferation and diversion, and the due diligence expected in trade finance.
objectives: Explain how export controls and dual-use regimes interact with financial sanctions
Identify proliferation financing and diversion risk in trade transactions
Apply proportionate due diligence to trade finance and goods-related payments
syllabus: Export control lists, dual-use goods and end-use controls
Proliferation financing obligations and the FATF standards
Trade finance red flags: goods, routes, pricing and parties
Common high-priority goods and diversion through third countries

modules.title: Correspondent Banking, Payments and Intermediaries
modules.summary: Sanctions risk in payment chains, correspondent relationships and intermediated business, including message transparency, nested relationships and reliance on others' controls.
objectives: Assess sanctions risk in correspondent, nested and intermediated relationships
Apply payment transparency standards and detect stripped or incomplete messages
Evaluate the limits of reliance on counterparties' screening
syllabus: Correspondent and nested relationships: due diligence and ongoing review
Payment message transparency, originator and beneficiary information
Rejecting versus blocking, and handling payments in transit
Fast payments, cross-border flows and real-time screening constraints

modules.title: Licensing, Frozen Assets, Investigations and Breach Reporting
modules.summary: What firms must do when they hold frozen assets or need a licence, how to investigate a potential breach, and how to report to the authority.
objectives: Manage frozen assets and reporting obligations correctly
Apply for, rely on and track general and specific licences
Investigate potential breaches and decide on voluntary disclosure
syllabus: Freezing, holding and reporting frozen funds and economic resources
General and specific licences, wind-down periods and licence conditions
Investigating a potential breach: facts, root cause and remediation
Reporting breaches and suspicions to the authority and the national FIU

modules.title: Governance, Risk Assessment, Testing and Assurance
modules.summary: Brings the programme together into a sanctions compliance framework the firm can evidence: risk assessment, policies, accountability, management information, testing and continuous improvement.
objectives: Build a sanctions risk assessment that drives proportionate controls
Test screening effectiveness and evidence assurance to the board and supervisors
Produce an action plan to strengthen the firm's sanctions framework
syllabus: Sanctions risk assessment, policy and senior management accountability
Screening tuning, data quality testing and model validation
Management information, horizon scanning and responding to new designations
Workshop: sanctions framework gap analysis and action plan

related.title: Crypto-Asset Financial Crime: Tracing and Controls for Compliance Teams
related.summary: A nine-module programme equipping compliance teams to detect crypto-asset financial crime, use blockchain analytics, meet travel rule and sanctions obligations, and investigate and report suspicion.

related.title: Financial Crime Compliance in the Age of AI
related.summary: A ten-module programme for MLROs and financial crime teams on the risk-based approach, AI-driven detection, AI-enabled threats and evidencing effectiveness to supervisors.

related.title: Fraud and Scams: Prevention, Detection and Response
related.summary: An eight-module practitioner programme on preventing, detecting and responding to fraud and scams, from authorised push payment scams and deepfakes to reimbursement and board reporting.

related.title: MLRO and Financial Crime Leadership
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving MLROs and deputies the tools to lead the firm's financial crime framework, report to the board and handle supervisory inspections.

related.title: The EU AML Package: AMLR, AMLD6 and AMLA (EU Edition)
related.summary: An eight-module programme on the EU AML package for supervisors and firms: the AML Regulation single rulebook, AMLD6, AMLA's supervisory model, crypto-asset transfers and transition planning.

related.title: Compliance Officer Academy
related.summary: A ten-module academy giving compliance officers the tools to run an independent, risk-based compliance function and handle supervisory engagement with confidence.
